newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks up sharply in morning, led by property.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks up sharply in morning, led by property.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks traded sharply higher in morning trade on Tuesday, led by a rally in the property sector ahead of a government land auction later.
The Hang Seng Index was up 103.36 points, or 0.81 percent, at 12,852.50. Turnover was HK$4.25 billion after the first hour of trade.
"The rise may be partly technical but there is no doubt that bargain hunters came into the market at the lower levels too," said Howard Gorges, a director at South China Brokerage.
"It does look as though we have some good results to look forward to from the property sector and the land auction looks as though it is going to be taken bullishly," he said.
The government is due to auction two plots of land at Ho Man Tin in Kowloon and Chai Wan on Hong Kong island on Tuesday. The auction is scheduled to start at 2:30 p.m. (0630 GMT).
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$1.25 to HK$72.00 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd gained HK$1.00 to HK$68.00.
New World Development Co Ltd, which is due to release its interim results later on Tuesday, gained HK$0.80 to HK$43.70.
Analysts said investors had also fully discounted a possible 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates at the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting later on Tuesday.
But Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities, said if the Fed raised interest rates by more than 25 basis points the market would be disappointed.
He also noted that futures were trading at a discount, which pointed to some lingering caution in the market. March Hang Seng futures were up 95 points at 12,810.
Shares in COSCO Pacific fell HK$0.15 to HK$10.35 after the company announced a HK$1.2 billion share placement.
